about: What develops in each pregnancy week, as body areas for the 3D baby. Each hotspot paraphrases the NHS Start for Life page for that same week; source ids resolve against size_weeks.json. Each fact is used in one week only. Survival and distress lines are left out.

hotspots.text: Your tiny embryo floats in a cushion of fluid, fed for now by a little yolk sac.
Its outer layer of cells will grow into the placenta, which brings oxygen and food later on.
The brain and spinal cord are forming fast.
The face is starting to take shape, with the beginnings of a tiny nose and eyes.
The first blood vessels are here, and a string of them will become the umbilical cord.
There is a little bump where the heart is growing.
Small limb buds have appeared, the start of arms and legs.
Tiny dents mark the spots where the ears will be.
A thin, see-through layer of skin covers the whole embryo.
The brain grows faster than the rest of the body, making about 100 new brain cells every minute.
Eyelids are beginning to grow over the eyes.
The arm buds are getting longer, and their flat ends will soon be tiny hands.
The head has started to uncurl a little.
The arms grow faster than the legs, because the upper body leads the way.
The legs are getting longer too, though knees and toes come later.
The face looks more like a face now, with eyelids, a little mouth and a tongue.
Hands and feet are forming, with small grooves where fingers and toes will be.
The first bones are starting to form.
The heart, lungs, kidneys and gut are all developing inside.
The heart beats about 180 times a minute, roughly three times faster than yours.
The eyes are half closed but can already react to light.
There is a delicate upper lip, two little nostrils, and tiny milk teeth waiting in the jaw.
Little jerky movements can be seen on a scan.
Fingers and toes are separating, and tiny fingernails are forming.
Miniature ears are taking shape.
Your baby is kicking already, weeks before you can feel it.
The skeleton is hardening from soft tissue into bone.
The heartbeat can now be picked up on an ultrasound scan.
The internal organs and muscles have grown a lot.
Movements are changing from jerky and random to more deliberate.
Some babies suck their thumb, which is practice for feeding later.
The head is getting rounder and more in proportion with the body.
Your baby swallows a little fluid, and the kidneys pass it back out as urine.
Your midwife may be able to hear the heartbeat with a handheld monitor.
A soft layer of fine hair called lanugo is starting to grow all over.
Eyebrows and eyelashes are starting to grow.
Hearing is beginning: your heartbeat and your tummy rumbles are the first sounds.
Your baby has started pulling faces, all at random for now.
The hands can make little fists.
The growing nervous system lets the arms and legs start to move.
Fingernails are growing, and the fingertips carry fingerprints that are unique, even between identical twins.
The eyes can move, though the eyelids stay shut for now.
Your baby can open and close their mouth.
Swallowing and sucking reflexes are developing this week.
The sense of touch is developing too.
There is a lot of wriggling, with arms and legs on the move.
Adult teeth are starting to form, lined up behind the first set.
Your baby keeps putting on weight, getting ready for birth.
A white, creamy coating called vernix now protects the skin.
Length is now measured head to heel, because the legs are no longer tucked out of view.
You may start to feel a flutter or bubbling, which could be your baby moving.
Your baby can hear voices from outside now, so singing to the bump counts.
Your baby now weighs more than the placenta, which keeps growing too.
Hair is starting to grow on the head.
The lungs are developing, and your baby practices breathing movements.
Swallowed fluid collects in the bowels and will become the first poo after birth.
Taste buds are developing and may be shaped by the flavors you eat.
The arms and legs are now in proportion with the body.
Over the next weeks you may see your tummy move when your baby kicks.
Everything is in proportion now. From here on it is mostly growing and maturing.
A loud noise may make your baby jump, and you might feel the odd hiccup.
The fluid around your baby is now mostly their urine, a warm cushion that keeps the temperature steady.
The eyes open for the first time around now, and blinking comes next. Eye color can keep changing for years.
Fat is filling out the folds of skin, so your baby looks less wrinkled.
All the organs keep maturing for life outside the womb.
The heart beats about 140 times a minute. A partner may hear it with an ear to the bump, if they find the right spot.
The creamy vernix coating starts to fade from now.
Every part is formed. The weeks ahead are for maturing and gaining fat.
The eyes can focus now. After birth your baby sees a face best from about 20 to 25 cm away.
Your baby is busy sucking fingers and turning the odd somersault.
Your baby is starting to recognize voices, so everyone can talk to the bump.
Your baby is fully formed, and the coming weeks are all about putting on weight.
The brain and nervous system are now fully developed.
The bones are hardening, except the skull, which stays soft so birth is a little easier.
Your baby is curled up with legs bent toward the chest.
Space is tight, but you can still see your bump change shape as your baby shifts.
Your baby is getting chubbier, which will help them stay warm after birth.
The lungs are probably mature enough to breathe without help.
Your baby can now suck and digest milk.
Your baby tries out expressions like frowning and smiling, at random for now.
By now you probably know when your baby is active and when they are calm.
Most of the soft lanugo hair is gone, though some babies keep a few patches.
The skin is growing a tougher outer layer that protects the organs and helps keep warm.
This is your due date week. Your baby is snug and keeps moving in their usual pattern.
